- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and prices are rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- If model shows strong upward trend after a recent spike, check for mean reversion; adjust downward 1–3% in next 3–5 days if sentiment weakens.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative mid-horizon, reduce forecast slope; avoid sharp upward revisions.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates > 3% from 14-day moving average, apply correction based on sentiment direction: bullish sentiment → +1% bias, bearish → -1% bias.
- If model forecast is > 5% above recent 7-day high, and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges turning points; use sentiment momentum (last 3 days) to adjust forecast slope.
